reasoning: I read the core docs, plans and todos in both sets in full. I sampled packets from each: A's split and system tasks (T06, T45) and B's spine and split tasks (T06, T37). I grepped the package docs for reference handling. Both sets are serious, well-built plans: per-window refits of the PCA reference, typed contracts from Pydantic to TypeScript, and the null-hypothesis-testing and data-analysis skills placed explicitly where they belong. Both also miss user requirements. Both route Sharadar through Nasdaq Data Link rather than api.sharadar.com, and both use SSE where the user asked for WebSocket. A drops the PPO trading agents and rules out the rented GPU ('Cloud compute; every model trains on the user's machine'). It also uses yfinance instead of yahooquery, and keeps a stale AD-03 that its own probe says fails. B drops the Yahoo cross-check entirely, along with the user's 10-name delisted reference check. A is ahead on structure and buildability. Its M1 is a richer end-to-end slice: download from the app with live progress, a company page and a universe page. Its roadmap puts each reference on the milestone it serves, and every packet's CONSTRAINTS.md exists. B's packets and AGENTS.md all point to a CONSTRAINTS.md that is not in the set. B's milestones are lopsided (M5 is tiny, M8 bundles portfolios, agents and the verdict), and its later roadmap milestones have no References lines. B's single cross-package interface task is cleaner than A's three parallel interface tasks that import one another, and B's walk-forward ledger design is very disciplined. On balance A is more buildable and better organised.

strengths: S2 is thorough: Marchenko–Pastur band, four estimators, min-variance, ERC and HRP, synthetic known-answer gates (SYNTH), and a family-corrected test of realized variance
S3 uses a planted-feature procedure check, a registered list and a one-shot holdout ledger

A frontend-design theme task gates every view
